arms.why: tau at the floor, so every lattice value clears it and every trial publishes a score: this is the arm F2-2 counts distinct values in and F1-18 tests for lattice membership, and its flip rate is F2-4's outside-below reading
tau at the second-smallest observed value, the only placement at which a decision can flip; F2-3 stratifies here because a purity test on a constant decision is vacuous

tau above the observed maximum: nothing is denied, and whether anything is LOGGED separates 'no finding, no score' from 'suppressed below tau' — which decides whether F2-3 is answerable on this surface at all

notes: tau_inside: degenerate_support — the harvest arm's support is the single value 4/5, so no INTERIOR tau exists. tau is placed AT that value, the only placement a one-point support admits. The flip rate is then insensitive to tau at EVERY placement, which is F2-4's sealed FALSE branch — measured here rather than inferred
tau_above: above — tau one lattice step above the observed maximum, so p = 0

publication_mechanism.M1: a finding is published and scored regardless of tau; tau selects the EFFECT
publication_mechanism.M2: the record is written only when the score clears tau, so every observable score belongs to a denial
publication_mechanism.consequence_for_f2_3: F2-3's stratum-purity test cannot fail on this surface — every observable score belongs to a denied request, so P(D=1|S=s)=1 for every observable s and a TRUE would be produced by the censoring, not by the service
